full_judgment:
Md Moinul Islam Chowdhury J : This Criminal Appeal was preferred by the convict appellants Abdul Haque Dakua and Jamal Sarder @ Md Jamal Sarder, against the Judgment and Order dated 5-6-2007 passed by the learned Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Damon Tribunal No. 2, Jhalakathi in Nari-o-Shishu Case No. 54 of 2001 arising out of Jhalakathi Police Station Case No. 9 dated 16-6-2001 corresponding to GR No. 93 of 2001 under sections 9(4)(Kha) and 30 of the Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Damon Ain, 2000 convicting the appellant No.1 and appellant No.2 under sections 9(4)(kha) and 30 of the Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Damon Ain, 2000 sentencing each of them to suffer rigorous imprisonment for 7 years and also to pay a fine of Taka 10,000 in default to suffer imprisonment for 1(one) year more. 

 2. The prosecution case, in short, is that the informant, Lovely Khanam, lodged an ejahar and a First Information Report (FIR) was filed at 16-45 hours on 16-6-2001 against both the appellants alleging, inter alia, that after divorce from her husband on 2-6-2001, there was an attempt to settle their disputes by some local people and the appellant No.1 being one of those people who used to go to the parental house of the informant and used to seduce her both through words and illegal proposal and demands as well as through gestures and also wanted to marry her. Being annoyed by his illicit activities the informant told appellant No.1 not to come to her residence. Thereafter, the appellant No.1 developed an intimacy with the informant's rival person within her village houses who is the appellant No. 2. The conducts of both the appellants appeared to be suspicious to the informant, thus she started to move carefully. At 8 Pm on 12-6-2001 at the veranda of her parental house while she was reading a book by the light of a hurricane lying on her bed, the appellants suddenly entered into her veranda. Having seen them she got by surprise and she screamed but the appellants told her to keep quiet and threatened her to kill her. The appellant No.1 came up on her body and the Appellant No. 2 held her mouth tight. Both of them started to touching and hurting her private parts of the body. The appellant No. 1 lifted her petticoat and attempted to rape her. In order to protect her, the informant managed to take a blade from underneath of the pillow of her bed and she struggled to get hold of the penis of the Appellant No.1 and with the said blade she inflicted a cut injury grievously on the penis of the appellant No. 1. At this point of time, the appellant No.1 asked the appellant No. 2, Jamal, to go out first as she has destroyed his life and then both the appellants run away from the place of occurrence but the Appellant No. 1 run away by holding his injured penis by the cloth. The appellants were known to the informant and she could recognize them by the light of the hurricane. On her hue and cry the informant's parents, sisters and other witnesses rushed to the place and they were informed of the occurrence from her. Being afraid of loss of prestige, the informant remained silent and the informant got the news that the appellant No. 1 was admitted in a hospital in Barisal and the delay to lodge this ejahar was due to the informant's being sick both physically and mentally. 

 3. The case was registered as Jhalakathi Police Station Case No. 9 dated 16-6-2001 under sections 9(4)(Kha) 30 of the Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Damon Ain, 2000, (the Ain, 2000). After, investigation into the matter the police submitted a final report as false being No.61 dated 19-8-2001 and the report contains a recommendation for initiating of proceeding under section 17 of the Ain, 2000 against the informant. Being aggrieved by the said final report dated 19-8-2001, the informant filed a Naraji Petition on 28-1-2002. The learned Tribunal allowed the Naraji on 5-3-2002 and ordered for further investigation into the case to be conducted by Detective Branch, Jhalakati. After further investigation into the case, the police again submitted a final report as false being No. 50 (Supplementary) dated 30-8-2003 containing another recommendation for initiating a proceeding under section 17 of the Ain, 2000 against the informant. It is stated that the informant again filed a Naraji petition dated 4-9-2003. The learned Tribunal by his order dated 11-10-2003 disregarded the final report (supplementary) dated 30-8-2003 and allowed the Naraji Petition by taking cognizance of the offence under sections 9(4)(kha) 30 of the Ain, 2000 against both the convict-appellants. 

 5. At the trial the prosecution examined as many as 7 (seven) witnesses in support of its case but the defense produced no witness. 

 6. The prosecution witness No.1 (the PW-1) Lovely Khanam, the informant of this case deposed in the Court on 11-5-2005 stating that on 12-6-2001 at about 8 PM the incident took place. She also deposed that there was a matrimonial dispute between her husband, Azizul Islam, and her and to settle the dispute many attempts were taken by the local people including the convict appellant No.1, Abdul Haque Dakua, who used to visit her house on the plea to settle the dispute with her husband. On one occasion the appellant No.1 said to her that it was not the settlement of dispute but he wanted to marry her. In this situation she asked him not to visit her any more, for which the appellant No. 1 threaten her to realize its consequences. On his threat, she started her day-to-day movements carefully. He also uttered some rude words to her on the street. The appellant No. 1, Abdul Haque Dakua, thereafter, built a friendship with the convict appellant No. 2 Jamal Sarder @ Md Jamal Sarder, who lives within the premises of her village house. On 12-6-2001 she was reading a book lying on her bed in the veranda of the house by the light of hurricane. The main door was open at that time. The convict-appellants entered into her room /veranda and she screamed on seeing them and sat from the laying down. The appellant No. 2 immediately shut her mouth by his hand when she tried to scream and the appellant No. 1 Abdul Haque Dakua, came on the bed and sat on her. Thereafter, the appellant No. 2 removed his hand from the mouth and hold her down tight and Abdul Haque Dakua, the appellant No. 1, thereafter, lifted her petticoat and attempted to enter his penis into her vagina but in the meantime, she managed to get a blade which was kept under the pillow of her bed and after a tough straggle with them she also managed to bring out the penis of Abdul Haque Dakua, by her left hand and caused a cut injury by the said blade by her right hand on the penis of the appellant No.1. Having sustained the said serious injury on his penis the appellant No. 1 screamed and said that his life has been destroyed by her and asked Jamal to escape, immediately thereafter, they left the room/ veranda. There is a dining room on the separate part of the house from her bed room where her parents and others were eating dinner. They came forward after hearing her screaming. She recognized the convict appellants by the light of the hurricane. Her parents could see and recognize the convicts when they were running away from the house thereafter, she described everything to them. In the cross this witness states that she is one of her eight sisters and she is the eldest among her sisters. She lived with her husband for two years and for a year she stayed separated and has been living with her parents. Her husband was unemployed after leaving the Job in a company who used to drink. After marriage her husband stayed in her parents' house for eight or nine months. She has a brother aged 12/13 years of old at that time when the incident took place. Within 2/3 months her husband left her house. There was a salish but nobody came to her for settlement except the appellant No. 1 who came to her house 2/3 times on the plea of settlement. She asked the appellant No. 1 if he had any proposal, to speak about it to her father. She also stated that how many children the appellant No. 1 had she did not know. Her parents did not scream because of shame but the convicts were recognized by the many people of the village when they were escaping from the place of occurrence. At the time of occurrence she was reading a book when other members of the family were having their dinner. The police could see blood on the bed sheet on her bed. When she used blade to cut penis of the appellant No. 1 blood dropped on share and on her right hand on her bed sheet. After sustaining the said injury the convict appellant No. 1 hold her penis by his lunge for which large amount of blood could not be dropped on her bed sheets and other bed cloths. She was threatened by a weapon. 

 7. She also stated that she filed two Naraji Petitions on submission of the final reports false by the police and she wanted to have an investigation by the DB police. On the incident DB police investigated and after two FRFs and two Naraji Petition the case started properly. PW-2 Roje, the sister of the informant deposed in the Court that both convict appellants were present at the dock. On 12-6-2001 at about 9 AM when she was having dinner with her parents she heard her sister's screaming and came to the corridor where two persons were running away and she could recognize them by the light of hurricane. She could see that her sister, the informant, was shaking and her clothes were misplaced and for a long time her sister could not say anything but she was shaking for some time. At that point of time her sister said that she caused a blade injury on the male part of the appellant No.1 Abdul Haque Dakua's body. In the cross examination this witness stated that there was no Salish. The convict appellants talk to her father about the settlement of disputes between her sister and her sister's husband. She denied that there was an enmity with the convicts of 20 years relating to a property. Her sister was overwhelmed after seeing suddenly to the convicts at their house. She could see a blade but the blade was not sought by the police. She could recognize the convict appellants when they were running away from the house by the light of hurricane. There was no affair between the convict No. 1 and her sister and the appellant No.1 had two children. 

 15. Mr Khan Saiful Rahman, the learned senior Advocate for the appellants submits before us that the impugned Judgment and Order of the conviction and sentence are bad in law as there are full of contradiction in the prosecution witnesses and evidence and the Tribunal failed to comprehend from the evidence and the materials on records that the prosecution has failed to prove its case beyond all reasonable doubt and, as such, the impugned order is liable to be set aside. 

 16. The learned Advocate also submits that from the order dated 11-10-2003, it appears that the learned Tribunal based its decision to allow the Naraji Petition on two separate medical reports one furnished by a Medical Board Jhalakati Sadar Hospital consisting of a Board three members and another furnished by one Dr. Subash Chandra Biswas. The first one was called for by the learned Tribunal to determine as to whether there is any mark of injury on the penis of the appellant No. 1. The second report was also called for by the Tribunal at the instance of appellants from the said Dr. Biswas, who said to have operated on the penis (male part of the body) of appellant No.1 for hydrocele on the left testis and one cyst on the penis on 20-8-2000, which proves that the prosecution case is not true, thus the Appeal is liable to be dismissed. 

 18. The learned Advocate further submits that the Medical experts were not sure as to which weapon caused the injuries on the penis of the convict appellant No. 1. Moreover, there is a Medical report submitted by one Dr Subash Chandra Biswas, stating that he operated up on the penis of the convict-appellant on 20-8-2000 for hydrocele of the left testis and one cyst on the penis of the appellant but the learned Tribunal without considering all the Medical documents in front him, came to a conclusion that the injury was caused by the blade as claimed by the informant. In support of his submission, the learned Advocate cited a case of State vs Mokbul Hossain,' 37DLR156, where upon this Court decided that a post mortem report cannot be used as a sufficient evidence when other evidence and conditions are sufficient to come to a decision and a post mortem report is to be excluded. 

 19. From the above decision the learned Advocate submitted that the Medical report submitted by the Medical board should not have used as an evidence against the convict appellants. He further submits that there are some embellishment in this case which “পেটের নিচে ৩/৪ টি কোপের দাগ”,”চোকির উপরে শোয়ানো” ”মুখ চেপে ধর” and the blade was not seized which caused the said injury, as such, the impugned Judgment and Order is not passed on the evidence in front of the learned Tribunal and, as such, there is no evidence to prove the case of the prosecution. 

 22. The learned Deputy Attorney General submits that the prosecution has adduced as money as seven witnesses in the trial who made consistent statements as to the incidents as it happened on 12-6-2001 at about 8 PM. It is also submitted that PW-1 Lovely Khanum, the informant-victim made a categorical allegation against the convict appellants alleging, inter alia, that the convict appellants No. 1 and 2 suddenly attacked the victim who was lying down on the bed and reading a book by the light of a hurricane. Having seen the appellants suddenly the victim tried to scream but the convict appellant No. 2 shut her mouth by his hand and the convict appellant No.1 sat on her body and thereafter, was pulling up her cloths and tried to commit an offence of rape. She further alleged that she could save herself from the offence of rape by causing an injury on the penis of the convict appellant No.1 Abdul Haque Dakua, which caused huge bleeding from the male part of his body and on her screaming both convict ran away. He further submits that her statements have been substantiated by the prosecution witness No. 7 in his deposition. The learned DAG further submits that the important phenomena of this case is that a woman cannot specifically say about an injury on the lower part of the penis of strange person unless she has caused it in herself defence. 

 25. He next submits that there are as many as two FRFs by the police and 2 Naraji petitioner against the said FRFs by the prosecution which means that the prosecution had to undertake a long course of sufferings to continue the proceeding against the present convict appellants because, in the meantime, there are as many as two Criminal Appeals being Criminal Appeal No. 707 of 2002 and the Criminal Appeal No. 4056 of 2003 and a Criminal Miscellaneous Case being No.8414 of 2002 filed by the present convict appellants in the High Court and all of which were dismissed/discharged. 

 30. After considering the submissions made by the learned Advocates for the parties and having perused the Memo of Appeal and the lower Court records, other materials of this case and the impugned Judgment of this case, it is apparent to us that the informant Lovely Khanum, filed an ejahar on 16-6-2001 alleging that the convict appellants suddenly went into her house at about 8 PM on 12-6-2001 while she was laying down on her bed and reading a book by the light of a hurricane which caused her to scream but her mouth was held tight by Jamal Sarder @ Md Jamal Sarder and the appellant No. 1, Abdul Haque Dakua, sat on her body and pulled up her under garments and tried to rape her by entering his erected penis in her and she straggled to get a blade kept under her pillow and pulled out the penis of the convict appellant No. 1 by her left hand and caught hold of it and she cut some of the lower part of the penis by the said blade by her right hand which caused serious injury to the convict appellant No.1 and caused him to scream. The injury caused secretion of huge quantity of blood but only some blood dropped on her share, blade and also on the bed shed because the convict appellant No.1 rapped the injured male part of his body by the lungi tightly and ran away from the place, therefore, enough blood could not drop on the place of occurrence. 

 32. In the examination-in-chief the prosecution witnesses No.1, Lovely Khanum, a very consistent statement which could not deviate her by the cross-examination on the part of the defense lawyer. It further appears from the records that there are two Final Reports as False (FRF) after investigation into the matter and there are two Naraji. The prosecution sought an investigation by the DB into the incident which was permitted by the learned Tribunal. The learned Tribunal in the proceeding of the case also inquired about the injury and sought a Medical report thereabout which appears from the order NO.30 dated 11-10-2003 of the learned Tribunal and which reads as follows:— 

 34. From the above it is apparent that the learned Tribunal was proceeding with the case in accordance with law. 

 37. Regarding the submissions of the learned senior Advocate for the convict appellants as to exclusion of a post mortem report when it is not sufficient evidence as it was decided by this Court in a case as reported in 37 DLR 156. We find that the above decision is not applicable in the present case as the Medical report submitted by the Medical Board pursuant to an order of the Court which is a vital evidence on the part of the prosecution to prove the case of injury inflected by the informant as her self defense and to save her from a heinous crime of rape. It also appears to us that the witness statements and the Medical report submitted by a Medical Board and also the deposition made by PW 7 cannot be excluded as claimed by the learned Advocate appearing for the convict appellants. 

 41. The impugned Judgment and Order passed on 5-6-2007 by the learned Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Damon Tribunal No. 2, Jhalakathi in Nari-o-Shishu Case No. 54 of 2001 arising out of Jhalakathi Police Station Case No. 9 dated 16-6-2001 corresponding to GR Case No. 93 of 2001 under sections 9)4)(Kha)30 of the Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Damon Ain, 2000 convicting the appellant No. 1 Abdul Haque Dakua under section 9(4)(kha) and the appellant No. 2 Jamal Sarder @ Md Jamal Sarder, under sections 9(4)(kha) 30 of the Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Damon Ain, 2000 sentencing each of them to suffer rigorous imprisonment for 7(seven) years and also to pay a fine of Taka 10,000 in default to suffer imprisonment for 1(one) year is hereby affirmed and upheld.
